   275	/**
   276	 * A declarative body-parsing route entry for {@link buildRoutes} and
   277	 * {@link dispatchRoute}.
   278	 *
   279	 * - `method` — HTTP method (uppercase).
   280	 * - `path` — Exact string path or a RegExp with named capture groups.
   281	 * - `handler` — Receives the parsed body (or `undefined` when `noBody` is
   282	 *   set), any named capture groups extracted from the RegExp match, and the
   283	 *   parsed query parameters from the request URL.
   284	 * - `statusCode` — Response status code (default `200`). Use `204` for empty
   285	 *   responses — the dispatcher writes the header and skips `sendJson()`.
   286	 * - `noBody` — When `true`, skip `readJsonBody()`.
   287	 */

   289	  method: string;
   290	  path: string | RegExp;
   291	  handler: (body: unknown, groups?: Record<string, string>, query?: URLSearchParams) => Promise<unknown>;

   293	  noBody?: boolean;
   294	}

   300	/**
   301	 * Guards against path-traversal attacks on URL parameters that are used as
   302	 * filesystem path segments.
   303	 *
   304	 * Rejects any segment that is empty or does not match {@link SAFE_SLUG_REGEX}
   305	 * (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/`). Throws {@link ApiError} `NOT_FOUND` so that
   306	 * callers receive the same status as a missing project — no information leak.
   307	 *
   308	 * @param segment - The raw URL parameter value to validate.
   309	 */
   310	function assertSafeSlug(segment: string): void {
   311	  if (!segment || !SAFE_SLUG_REGEX.test(segment)) {
   312	    throw new ApiError('NOT_FOUND', 'Invalid repo or slug parameter.');
   313	  }
   314	}
